title: Recording as Josephine Beatty; Bailey and Todd, Clarence Williams
summary: She used her sister's name because of her Paramount contract; talk of the record with Bailey and Todd, "Cakewalking Babies" and sessions with Williams, Bechet and Armstrong.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The reason you used your sister's Josephine Beatty was because you were under name, (inaudible) contract?
To Paramount. So you used it when you did Sennett, for instance?
Yes, when I used Josephine Beatty's name I was under contract for Paramount. That's why I used her name.
Let's see, now, who were you singing --

Beatty
Tod -- Bailey and Todd?
Oh, Mr. Todd, yes.
Tell me about Buster Todd.
Yeah, what was his name? Mr. Todd. Now, he wrote a song, what was his song. You put the name of his song down there?
You did "Cakewalking Babies" with him.
Yeah, I did "Cakewalking Babies" with (unintelligible). Wait a minute, what's that other song? His song, what was his song?
We can find that. (inaudible).
Yeah. Well, I know Mr. Todd. Yeah, I did that with him. And somebody else. I was trying to think --
You recorded with Clarence Williams Blue Five too (inaudible).
"Cakewalking Babies", what was that -- Jack Palmer's song. It will have to come to me later. I can't think of that.
"Nobody Knows the Way I Feel this Morning" (inaudible). Was around that time, too.
Yeah, uh-huh.
But I remember the Gennett record, Beatty Bailey and Todd.
Yes, indeed.
Wasn't it Louie and Sidney Bechet and Clarence Williams?
Clarence Williams, Sidney Bechet, and Louis Armstrong. And who was on guitar? Wasn't somebody on guitar with me?
I don't remember. I have all that information.
You got all information. Uh-huh.
